desc: Ideate and select the core algorithm (right-endpoint sweep with active top-two values).

Implement the right-endpoint sweep: normalize pairs to (a,b) with a<b, bucket by b, insert pairs with b==r before counting, maintain largest a, its owner id and multiplicity, and second-largest distinct a (0 if absent), accumulating base += r-largest and per-owner gain (largest-second) when multiplicity==1.
Execute the solution on Example 1 (got 9) and Example 2 (got 12); both match expected outputs.

Cross-check against an independent brute-force solver on 20000 random small inputs (n in 2..8) covering duplicates, reversed pairs, tied a-values, a single pair, and never-bottleneck pairs; zero mismatches reported.
No mismatch found, so no fallback (left-endpoint sweep / Fenwick top-two query) was needed.
